chapter_note: This chapter is almost entirely systematic cosmological logistics: foreprepared containment-places for hostile beings and wastes, expressed in impersonal, process-oriented voice (“Before X…, a place was constructed…”). No dialogue frame, no Gospel/NT citation, and no institutional/pastoral application. A few motifs (watchers/giants) may reflect later syncretic mythic material within Manichaean cosmology, but the diction remains within the cosmic system rather than pointing to contemporary institutions.

paragraphs.core_text: Understand also this other (matter): Before these vessels were discharged and swept down from heaven, first three ditches were fashioned and constructed for them, in which they would be bound and fettered.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal expository teaching; purely cosmological sequencing (“Before… first…”) describing prepared containment within the cosmic architecture.

paragraphs.core_text: Before the sea giant was discharged from the sphere, the Father of Life constructed a place for [him i]n this great sea that is within the walls, whereon the ships sail, and where the fullness shall [ ... ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic geography and beings (Father of Life; sea giant; great sea within the walls). Register scores undercount cosmological vocabulary here, but the content stays entirely within the system.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, before the [ ... ] was displayed to the worlds [ ... ] the earth [ ... ... f]ell to the sea and its thought shaped it, the Father of Life constructed a place for it in [the ... ... ] below the four mountains, above the mountains of the heavens above [ ... ] that [ ... ] a great plain it digs in Matter in the midst of the worlds. When the Adamant of Light was sent to it, he hastened after it to that place, smote it and threw it between mountains in the place made ready for it [ ... ] is set fast upon it till the end of the universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core mythic-cosmological mechanics: prepared place, layered mountain cosmography, and intervention by a named cosmic agent (Adamant of Light). No application to contemporary institutions.

paragraphs.core_text: Before the waste and dirt of the darkness were swept out from creation, gehennas were constructed in which the waste might be covered till the dissolution of the universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Functional cosmological infrastructure (“gehennas” as containment for cosmic waste) and eschatological endpoint (“dissolution of the universe”); still impersonal and system-internal.

paragraphs.core_text: Before the rebels rose up, they whose corps rebelled in the ruling-power above and below, they [ ... ] outside, and also the tyrants in whose heart it lay [to ty]rannise amongst the murk and the clouds and winds and spirits and storms; for them were constructed in the great outer sea seven hostels, places whence they are thrown into the depths and the darkness [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Sevenfold architectural provision (“seven hostels”) for cosmic rebels; the list of domains (murk, clouds, winds, spirits, storms) remains cosmological rather than institutional.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, before the abortions [fell ... ...] to the earth, there was set apart [ ... ]: they are gathered in and dwell therein.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Brief but consistent with the chapter’s repetitive cosmological template: pre-set place for a class of beings; no frame or exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, before the watchers rebelled and came down from heaven, a prison was fashioned and constructed for them in the depths of the earth, below the mountains.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Uses the same systematic “Before…, a place was constructed…” pattern. ‘Watchers’ motif may be inherited from older Jewish myth cycles, but here it functions as integrated cosmic-history teaching (still system-internal).

paragraphs.core_text: Before the children of the giants were born, they who had [no] knowledge of righteousness in them nor divinity, thirty-six cities were assigned and constructed for them wherein the children of [the giants would] live; they who would come to beget from each other, they who shall spend ten hundred years alive.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the containment/assignment schema with a numbered structure (“thirty-six cities”). The moral phrasing (“knowledge of righteousness… nor divinity”) slightly shifts register and may reflect later mythic-ethical coloration, but it does not pivot to church discipline or contemporary targets, and it remains embedded in cosmic history.
